name: El Tour de Tucson
start_location: Tucson Convention Center and surrounding streets, downtown Tucson (260 S Church Ave, Tucson, AZ 85701)
date_note: The 43rd El Tour de Tucson is Saturday, November 21, 2026. Packet pickup and the expo are at the Tucson Convention Center in the days before.
founded_by: Richard J. DeBernardis, a touring cyclist who later formed Perimeter Bicycling Association of America
registration_note: Registration opens roughly a year out and prices rise monthly: $125 through April 30, $135-$175 May through September, $185-$300 in October and November (2026 adult pricing). Riders 17 and under are free. Fees are non-refundable and non-transferable; distance changes are free until October 18, then $25. The event does not run a lottery.

distances.label: 62 miles (Metric Century)
distances.note: 9:00 am start; 1,600+ ft of climbing. Some materials list it as 63 miles

terrain: Paved roads through the Sonoran Desert: Davis-Monthan AFB, Old Spanish Trail past Saguaro National Park East and Colossal Cave, then Vail, Sahuarita and Green Valley before returning downtown
participants: about 10,000 riders a year, per the organizer
cost: $125-$300 for adults depending on registration date (2026 pricing); youth 17 and under free
summary: El Tour de Tucson is a timed charity ride held in Tucson, Arizona, on the Saturday before Thanksgiving, with 102-, 62- and 32-mile routes that all start and finish at the Tucson Convention Center. It began in 1983 with fewer than 200 riders and now draws about 10,000 a year. Perimeter Bicycling, the nonprofit that runs it, says the ride has helped raise more than $138 million for charities since it started. The 2026 edition is November 21.
history: Richard J. DeBernardis started the first Perimeter bicycling event in Tucson in 1983, after riding 2,218 miles from Alaska to Mexico in 40 days. That first ride had fewer than 200 cyclists and raised $4,500. A second event followed in 1986, and Perimeter Bicycling Association of America was formed around it.

El Tour became the flagship. The organizer describes it as the largest cycling fundraiser in America, with more than 311,000 riders across all Perimeter events over the years. In 2019 the charities riding with the event passed $100 million raised in total; by 2025 the figure was over $138 million. The 2026 ride is the 43rd.
The event now supports more than 120 nonprofits a year through fundraising teams. Riders can enter on their own or through a charity team at a reduced fee.
what_to_expect: All routes start and finish at the Tucson Convention Center downtown. The century leaves at 7:00 am, the metric at 9:00 am and the 32-miler at 10:00 am. Timing is by chip on your bib and a second tag on the seatpost; your clock starts when you roll across the start line. Experienced pack riders on the 102 and 62 can apply for a Platinum corral.

Aid stations come roughly every 7-12 miles. The route closes at 4:30 pm, and aid stations shut down on a schedule that lets riders finish by then; there is no support or recorded time after that. Every finisher gets a medallion. CPSC-approved helmets are mandatory, aerobars are not allowed, and pedal-assist e-bikes ride in their own category without awards.

The century heads out past Davis-Monthan Air Force Base, along Old Spanish Trail with saguaro views near Colossal Cave, then swings south through Vail, Sahuarita and Green Valley before coming back into the city. Expect a cool start and a warm, dry afternoon.
weather_note: Late November in Tucson is mild and dry. Around November 20 the average daily high is about 72 F and the low about 48 F, with roughly an 8 percent chance of rain on any given day. Dress for a cold 7 am start and a warm afternoon.

faq.q: When is El Tour de Tucson 2026?
faq.a: Saturday, November 21, 2026. It is always the Saturday before Thanksgiving.
All routes start and finish at the Tucson Convention Center downtown. The century starts at 7:00 am, the metric at 9:00 am, the 32-miler at 10:00 am.
Adult entries were $125 through April 30, 2026, rising monthly to $185-$300 in October and November. Riders 17 and under are free. Fees are non-refundable.
The route closes at 4:30 pm. After that there is no course support and no recorded finish time.
Pedal-assist only, no throttle. E-bikes have their own category, cannot use the Platinum corral and are not eligible for placement awards.

faq.q: Where do I get my packet?
faq.a: Only at the expo at the Tucson Convention Center, using the QR code from your confirmation email. A proxy can pick it up with your QR code and a photo ID.
